Read-only audit of release bf088769 against development 1f8b6077 (condensed into 8251007). No validation, builds, tests, edits, or GitHub mutations performed.

Concrete release defect

  • P1: Documentation publication can report success without updating GitHub Pages. Release .github/workflows/docs.yml:90-114 pushes Mike output using ${{ github.token }}, while RELEASING.md:42-46 requires Pages deployment from gh-pages. GitHub explicitly documents that pushes using GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger Pages builds. Consequently publish-release.yml:126-139 can advance from “Publish versioned documentation” to the GitHub/PyPI release with stale or absent live documentation. Keep versioned Mike output, but explicitly upload and deploy the complete versioned site using the native Pages actions already present in development .github/workflows/docs.yml:39-59. Verify the live URLs afterward. Sources: GitHub token behavior, Pages publishing configuration.

Required reconciliation work

  1. Port wheel smoke tests to the final API; neither side can be selected wholesale. Release deletes development’s scripts/check_wheel.py, replacing it with scripts/smoke_wheel_install.py. The latter still calls removed or renamed APIs:

    • plane_wave(..., polarization="positive_helicity") at release smoke lines 134–136 versus pol= in development CHANGELOG.md:142-147;
    • SMatrix._from_array at lines 155/181 versus solve_periodic(...).to_smatrix(...);
    • lattice.expansion_with_context at line 394 versus diff.lattice_expansion;
    • diff.wigner, diff.periodic_from_table, advect.periodic_conversion, kind= special-function selectors, and TMatrix._assemble.

    The authoritative replacement inventory is development CHANGELOG.md:99-145,174-193; development’s existing wheel checker already incorporates many replacements.

  2. Retain optimized floating-point-environment verification. Development scripts/check_wheel.py:44-59 exercises scripts/float_environment.py against the installed optimized wheel, checking bitwise equality for ordinary versus denormal-flushing callers. Release’s replacement smoke script has no such check. Copying the release replacement would silently drop this substantive regression check. Port it into the combined smoke, including the existing x86-64/AArch64 support assertion.

  3. Separate ordinary test helpers from the unavailable oracle before extending Python support. Development tests/_support.py:14 imports treams unconditionally. Numerous nested API, adapter, and native-boundary tests import _support for ordinary helpers. Release tests/conftest.py:185-190 follows sibling modules only, so it misses tests/_support.py when inspecting nested tests; those collections will fail on 3.14/3.15. Merely teaching it to find the shared helper would instead skip many tests that do not need the oracle. Move oracle imports into the actual oracle helpers, then reconcile conditional collection and explicitly report remaining skips. Preserve the stronger 3.12/3.13 oracle coverage.

  4. Preserve development’s test categories and CI property-test budget. Development tests/conftest.py:24-28,31-54 owns Hypothesis profiles and category registration; development CI sets HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci at .github/workflows/ci.yml:78-81. Release CI does not set it. Retaining development conftest with release CI silently reduces properties from 100 to 30 examples. New release tests also need the applicable category because development tests/test_suite_rules.py:24-29 rejects uncategorized tests. Combine conftest hooks instead of overriding one version.

  5. Reconcile command names, paths, generators, and workflow checks.

    • Development uses just ci; release documentation directs users to just verify. Establish one authoritative command and update both release instructions.
    • Replace references to scripts/generate_agent_docs.py, tests/test_docs.py, tests/test_support.py, and docs/api.md with development’s actual generator/test layout.
    • Preserve development formal-workflow path filters for moved Rust modules; retain release’s checksum-verified elan installer.
    • Preserve development rustdoc generation and add it to each versioned documentation build.
    • Retain Material and remove the release branch’s custom theme, hooks, and browser-shell checks as explicitly directed by HANDOFF.md:25-32,100-105.
    • Consolidate RELEASING.md and development docs/development/releasing.md so release instructions cannot diverge.

  6. Reconcile metadata and dependency policy together. Retain the approved 0.1.0 Cargo version authority, release’s CPython 3.12–3.15 declaration, dependency-floor/latest testing, bundled licenses, Cargo dependency policy, and build-path remapping. Retain development-specific lint exceptions, test configuration, Material dependency, project naming, and URLs. Relock once the final graph is settled and regenerate the license bundle against that exact graph/toolchain. Do not reuse the existing bundle after silently selecting a different lock file.

  7. Port the release numerical changes into development’s moved modules. HANDOFF.md:83-99 identifies the clean-room Ferrers implementation, regression cases, spherical-polar property correction, and current-toolchain Clippy fixes. Preserve the clean-room provenance constraint when assigning the Ferrers port. Requalify at the final source revision rather than treating the handoff’s draft port as complete.

  8. Finish small public-facing omissions. Development still has no treams_rs.__version__; its __main__.py:16 leaves argparse’s program name implicit. These remain the handoff’s small follow-ups. Remove HANDOFF.md and handoff/ once their required information is incorporated; extract the separate SciPy report material before deleting its only copy.

Release machinery worth retaining

The release branch already supplies useful, coherent mechanisms:

  • A 20-wheel family: CPython 3.12–3.15 across Linux x86-64/ARM64, macOS Intel/ARM64, and Windows x86-64; plus an sdist rebuilt into an installed wheel.
  • Fresh installed-wheel base/Advect/HDF5 profiles, simultaneous dependency minimums, archive/metadata/license validation, build-path scans, checksums, and an immutable-source manifest.
  • TestPyPI verification before production approval; annotated tag verification; publication of the same candidate artifacts.
  • A successful main push CI run for the exact candidate SHA, enforced by .github/scripts/verify-release-state.sh:64-99.
  • Pinned actions, least-privilege publishing jobs, OIDC publishing, checksum-verified downloaded executables, and a full-history secret scan.

I did not find another independently established fatal publishing defect beyond the Pages mechanism. The substantial remaining risks are integration and unexecuted hosted qualification.

Qualification and hosted prerequisites

After approval, a draft integration PR targeting main can run the complete nonpublishing CI and wheel family: release CI’s pull-request trigger invokes reusable native-wheel builds. Publishing workflows do not need to be merged first merely to qualify distributions.

Required evidence before calling the integration ready:

  • Exact rewritten integration revision passes Rust/MSRV/stable checks, Python suites and dependency matrices, generated-doc checks, applicable formal checks, licenses, secrets, and the complete hosted wheel/sdist family.
  • Optimized wheel smoke includes the final API and floating-point-mode checks.
  • Material documentation is rendered and visually inspected; versioned Pages output is actually deployed and checked.
  • Release source/metadata/installed __version__ agree; wheel and sdist contents contain no temporary handoff material.
  • Performance claims affected by numerical/concurrency changes are requalified on a suitable idle host.
  • After the eventual merge, the resulting main SHA needs its own successful push CI; pre-rewrite or PR merge-commit evidence cannot satisfy the publisher’s identity requirement.

Parent’s live settings audit supplies the remaining hosted blockers: repository is private; main protection/tag rules are absent; the separate release approval environment is missing. Existing pypi and testpypi environments are not substitutes for it. Configure the documented release reviewer gate, immutable version-tag protection, trusted/pending publishers, Codecov access, corrected Pages deployment, and private vulnerability reporting before publication.

The handoff reports extensive local passes at 46f36fe, including 2,386 Python tests, but explicitly excludes hosted macOS/Windows/ARM64 wheels, Codecov, TestPyPI/PyPI, and Pages. Those statements are historical claims, not proof for the reconciled or rewritten branch.
